title: Expand exercise library with 20 exercises per muscle group, routine builder, and form videos

requirements.text: Expand the backend exercise data to include approximately 20 real, factual exercises per muscle group (covering all existing muscle groups: chest, back, shoulders, biceps, triceps, legs, glutes, core, forearms, calves). Each exercise must include: name, targeted muscle group, a concise list of benefits (3–5 bullet points with accurate physiological/functional benefits), a description of correct form/technique, difficulty level, equipment needed, and at least one image URL and one video URL demonstrating correct form. All exercise names, benefits, and descriptions must be accurate and based on well-established exercise science.

quotes: each muscle group has about 20 different exercise images and text of the name of workout and benefits
Each workout must be real and factual and demonstrate precision for customer learning

acceptanceCriteria: Each of the 10 muscle groups has at least 20 distinct, real exercises stored in the backend.
Every exercise record contains: name, muscleGroup, benefits (array of strings), description, imageUrls (array), videoUrls (array), difficulty, and equipment fields.
All exercise names and benefits are accurate and match established fitness/exercise science.
No placeholder or fictional exercises exist in the dataset.

requirements.text: Generate semi-realistic to realistic exercise illustration images for each exercise. Each image should clearly depict the human body performing the specific exercise with proper form, using a semi-realistic to realistic art style (not cartoonish). Images should show muscle engagement visually. Produce one image per exercise (approximately 200 total across all muscle groups).

quotes: Image and video types should be semi realistic to realistic

acceptanceCriteria: Each exercise displayed in the workout library has a distinct, semi-realistic to realistic image.
Images are stored as static assets under frontend/public/assets/generated.
Images clearly depict a human performing the labeled exercise with correct form.

requirements.text: Update the WorkoutLibraryPage to display all exercises for each muscle group in a grid or list layout. Each exercise card must show: (1) the exercise image in a semi-realistic to realistic style, (2) the exercise name prominently, and (3) a concise benefits summary. Cards must be visually polished and consistent across all muscle groups.

quotes: each muscle group has about 20 different exercise images and text of the name of workout and benefits

acceptanceCriteria: All ~20 exercises per muscle group are visible when the muscle group section is expanded.
Each card shows the exercise image, exercise name, and 3–5 benefit points.
The layout is responsive and consistent across all muscle groups.
No exercises are cut off or hidden without a clear 'show more' interaction.

requirements.text: Make each exercise card clickable to open a detail modal or drawer. The modal must display: the exercise name, full benefits list, correct form description, equipment needed, difficulty level, and an embedded video clip demonstrating correct form. Video URLs should support YouTube embeds and direct video files. The modal should have a clear close button.

quotes: Each exercise will be clickable to show sample video clips of correct form

acceptanceCriteria: Clicking any exercise card opens a modal or drawer without navigating away from the page.
The modal displays the full exercise name, benefits, form description, equipment, difficulty, and an embedded video.
YouTube URLs are rendered as embedded iframes; direct video URLs use an HTML5 video player.
The modal can be dismissed via a close button or clicking outside it.

requirements.text: Implement a workout routine builder feature. Users must be able to click an 'Add to Routine' button on each exercise card to add it to a personal workout routine. The routine should be displayed in a collapsible sidebar or bottom panel showing all selected exercises. Users can remove exercises from the routine. The routine should be saveable (persisted to the backend for authenticated users, or stored in localStorage for guests).

quotes: Customers will be able to choose workouts for their workout routines

acceptanceCriteria: Each exercise card has an 'Add to Routine' button that adds the exercise to the active routine.
A routine panel/sidebar shows all exercises currently in the routine with remove controls.
Authenticated users can save and reload their routine via the backend.
Guest users have their routine persisted in localStorage for the session.
Duplicate exercises are not added twice; a visual indicator shows when an exercise is already in the routine.

requirements.text: Add backend support for storing and retrieving user workout routines. A routine must include: a name, an ordered list of exercise IDs, and the user's principal ID. Support creating, reading, updating, and deleting routines per user.

quotes: Customers will be able to choose workouts for their workout routines

acceptanceCriteria: Backend exposes functions: createRoutine, getMyRoutines, updateRoutine, deleteRoutine.
Each routine is scoped to the calling user's principal.
Routines store an ordered list of exercise IDs and a routine name.
Calling getMyRoutines returns only routines belonging to the authenticated caller.

constraints: All exercise data must be real, factual, and based on established exercise science — no fictional or invented exercises.
Video embeds must support YouTube iframes and direct video file URLs, consistent with existing media rendering in WorkoutLibraryPage and BlogPostPage.
Do not modify files under frontend/src/hooks/ or frontend/src/components/ui.
Maintain the existing spa/dark aesthetic and Tailwind design system.
nonGoals: Live streaming or real-time video features.
Third-party fitness API integrations (e.g., Wger, Fitbit).
AI-generated or personalized workout plan recommendations.
Payment gating for the routine builder feature (unless already gated by membership logic).
